email.subject: Last chance to collect your parcel

body.v: Your parcel has been waiting at the pick-up point for 6 days. It will go back to the sender tomorrow if it is not collected.
Collecting it costs nothing. Bring your ID and the code shown in the ParcelPoint app.
You can see the opening hours in the app.

hotspots.explain: The address is on parcelpoint.example, the real domain.
This is a real deadline, but it asks nothing of you except to collect your parcel. Urgency alone does not make an email a scam.
Collecting costs nothing. A scam would ask for a fee here.
It sends you to the app you already have, not to a link.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: ParcelPoint: the address is on the real domain and everything points to the app.

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: Some urgency, since the parcel goes back tomorrow. But the pressure is a real deadline, not a trick.
choices: Some urgency, from a real deadline

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Collect your parcel in person. There is no payment, no login and no link.
choices: Collect the parcel, at no cost

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Open the ParcelPoint app yourself to see the pick-up point and the code. The email points you there.
choices: Click a link in the email
Reply and ask for more time

actions.label: Open the ParcelPoint app yourself and look at the pick-up details
actions.consequence: The parcel and its collection code are listed.

actions.label: Collect the parcel from the pick-up point
actions.consequence: You hand over your ID and the code. No money is asked for.

actions.label: Reply to offer to pay for an extension
actions.consequence: The no-reply address does not answer. Nothing was needed anyway.

attacker_reveal: This one is real, dear, even though it has a deadline. The domain is right, nobody asks for money and it sends you to the app. A deadline alone is not a red flag. Ask what they want from you.
